stories.title: YouTube doubles the watch-hour requirement to start earning ad revenue
stories.summary: YouTube has raised the bar for creators trying to qualify for its Partner Program, now requiring roughly twice as many watch hours as before to start earning money, according to reports from Engadget, TechCrunch, and The Verge. The exact new threshold and rationale weren't detailed, but the change makes it noticeably harder for new creators to reach monetization.
stories.whyItMatters: YouTube remains the dominant platform for video creators, so any tightening of monetization eligibility reshapes the economics of building a channel from scratch.
whatToWatch: Creator community reaction and whether YouTube clarifies its reasoning
Whether subscriber-count requirements change alongside watch hours
questions: Is this aimed at ad-revenue quality control or spam/low-effort content?
Does it apply retroactively to creators close to the old threshold?

stories.title: Cold Iron Studios shuts down cloud version of a $60 game, no refunds offered
stories.summary: Developer Cold Iron Studios is shutting down the cloud-streamed version of a $60 game without offering refunds to affected players, according to Ars Technica. Details on which title and why the shutdown is happening weren't specified in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another example of buyers losing access to paid software they thought they owned once a publisher pulls the plug on server-dependent infrastructure.
